name: Abacavir
drug_class: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI; carbocyclic guanosine analogue)
route_note: oral tablet or solution once or twice daily; HLA-B*57:01 screening required before starting
originator: Glaxo Wellcome (building on carbocyclic nucleosides from Robert Vince, University of Minnesota)

discovery.by: Glaxo Wellcome, from carbovir work by Robert Vince (University of Minnesota)
discovery.note: Prodrug-like analogue of carbovir with better oral absorption and brain penetration.

tagline: HIV drug that made pharmacogenetic screening (HLA-B*57:01) routine
summary: Abacavir is a carbocyclic nucleoside analogue that is converted inside cells to carbovir triphosphate, a blocker of HIV reverse transcriptase. A serious hypersensitivity reaction strongly linked to the HLA-B*57:01 allele made it one of the first drugs for which genetic testing became standard before use. It is widely used in children and in combination tablets such as Triumeq.
mechanism: Abacavir is converted by adenosine phosphotransferase and a cytosolic deaminase to carbovir monophosphate, then by cellular kinases to carbovir triphosphate, a guanosine analogue.
Carbovir triphosphate competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate for HIV reverse transcriptase and terminates the DNA chain. Resistance involves mutations such as K65R, L74V, Y115F and M184V.
The hypersensitivity reaction occurs because abacavir binds within the peptide-binding groove of the HLA-B*57:01 molecule, changing the self-peptides presented and triggering a T-cell response.
uses: HIV-1 infection in adults and children in combination with other antiretrovirals

history.title: HLA link
history.detail: Two groups (Mallal et al. and Hetherington et al.) report the strong association between HLA-B*57:01 and abacavir hypersensitivity.

history.title: Combination
history.detail: Abacavir/lamivudine (Kivexa/Epzicom) is approved as a once-daily tablet.

history.title: PREDICT-1
history.detail: A randomised trial shows prospective HLA-B*57:01 screening eliminates immunologically confirmed hypersensitivity; the same year the D:A:D cohort reports an association with myocardial infarction.

history.title: Triumeq
history.detail: Abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine is approved as a single-tablet regimen.

pk.half_life: about 1.5 h in plasma; intracellular carbovir triphosphate about 21 h
pk.metabolism: alcohol dehydrogenase and glucuronyl transferase to inactive metabolites (not CYP)

serious: multi-organ hypersensitivity reaction (fever, rash, gastrointestinal and respiratory symptoms), which can be fatal on rechallenge
possible increased risk of myocardial infarction
safety.boxed_warning: Serious and sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions, more common in patients with HLA-B*57:01; screen before starting and never restart after a suspected reaction (US label).

facts: Abacavir was among the first drugs where routine pharmacogenetic testing prevented a serious adverse reaction.
HLA-B*57:01 is carried by roughly 5–8% of people of European descent and is less common in many African populations.

references.title: Mallal S et al. HLA-B*5701 screening for hypersensitivity to abacavir (PREDICT-1). NEJM 2008
